_comment: IMPERSONATIONHUNT PERMUTATION TABLES — the search space `--hunt-impersonation` sweeps when hunting lookalikes of a seed brand. This is the file to tune per campaign: add the TLDs a ring is actually using, or the affixes it bolts onto the brand, and the next hunt covers them. Bigger tables = more candidates = more crt.sh/DNS lookups, and generate_variants caps the total at max_variants (default 600), so the nearest-first ordering matters: typo -> combosquat -> TLD sweep.

tld_sweep._comment: TLDs the brand label is swapped across. Curated scam-heavy + common list, NOT the full IANA set — a full sweep would blow the candidate cap on TLDs no fraud ring uses. Multi-part suffixes (co.uk, com.vn) are fine.

combo_affixes._comment: Affixes an operator bolts onto a brand to make a combosquat (login-<brand>.com, <brand>-wallet.com). Applied as both prefix and suffix, with and without a hyphen.

qwerty_adjacency._comment: Physical QWERTY neighbours per character, used to bound fat-finger insertion/replacement to plausible typos instead of the whole alphabet. Key = character, value = string of its neighbours. Add a row to support another keyboard layout.

homoglyphs._comment: Single-character ASCII visual confusables. Key = character, value = list of characters it can be swapped for (rn/vv style multi-char pairs go in homoglyph_sequences). ASCII only by design — the engine asserts every generated candidate is ASCII, so Unicode/IDN confusables belong in a punycode hunt, not here.

homoglyph_sequences._comment: Multi-character visual confusable pairs as [from, to] — 'm' rendered as 'rn', 'w' as 'vv'. Both directions must be listed explicitly if you want both.
